div.h1: Both halves of the system are ALREADY the same machine
div.p: A type interns VALUES by a column tuple. A rel interns NAMES by a (parent, local_name, arity) tuple. In both, SQLite's UNIQUE constraint IS the hash-cons, and the INTEGER PRIMARY KEY rowid IS the interned id.
a declared type, e.g. rel file(repo: text, at: fpath)
a module, e.g. rel orchard { ... }, a rel with children

div.p: UNIQUE (cols) -- SQLite refuses the duplicate

g.text: what happens on a name collision?

div.p: THROW rel_name_collision -- does not exist yet
Putting h_schema INSIDE the table name makes every column edit a RENAME. A rename in SQLite is a NEW EMPTY TABLE, so the rows are orphaned and unreachable.
Rust hashes the crate, never the item body, for exactly this reason.
file B changes on disk recompile file B ALONE -> a list of rels, each with its four hashes

div.p: h_id not present CREATE TABLE seed rows consumers: RED
h_schema differs DROP TABLE + CREATE rows are lost, on purpose consumers: RED
h_schema same, h_rule differs keep the table DELETE FROM + recompute consumers: check h_rows
all four hashes equal touch NOTHING no DDL, no rows, no wake
was in __rel, absent now refcount -> 0 DROP TABLE consumers: RED

g.text: the rel graph after file B is reshaped

div.h1: the stop rule (this is the whole optimization)
div.p: ripe recomputed, and its NEW h_rows came out EQUAL to its old h_rows.
So report never runs. Red stops travelling the moment recomputation produces identical rows.
This is red/green marking, and the repo already has the law that demands the digest.
A red rel on a CYCLE of the level graph makes the WHOLE cycle red at once. Half an SCC cannot be green.
rename __catalog_rel -> __rel (+ its index)
